_comment: An EXAMPLE verification rule set. Nothing in Vision OS references this file,
and deleting it changes no behaviour — absent a document, no verification
policy is built and the trigger policy is the unwrapped default.
WHAT THIS DOCUMENT IS FOR. A closed-set detector scores a fixed vocabulary
and returns the best of it. Shown an object it was never trained on, it must
still spread probability across the words it knows, and the winner is the
nearest neighbour rather than an identification. A pen scores 0.454 as
'toothbrush' — comfortably above any threshold that still admits real
detections. No confidence floor fixes that, because the number is not wrong;
the question was.
So these rules say when a class claim needs corroborating from a second
source, and — far more often — when it does not. The second half is the
expensive one to get wrong: a rule that matches everything turns one demand
into one model call per object per freshness window.
READ THE CONDITIONS AS 'OR'. Any one firing warrants a look. A claim is
doubtful if it is ambiguous, OR outside the model's vocabulary, OR unstable
over time; requiring all three at once would let the pen through because it
happened to be stable.
Governs the corroborating attribute only. Every other demand — the PPE
attributes, the activity, the colours — falls through untouched, which
is what keeps ordinary understanding unchanged.
detector_label_space limits this rule to closed-set detectors. An
open-vocabulary model is scored against labels supplied at query time,
so its silence carries information a closed-set silence does not, and
the same low score means something different.
An UNDECLARED label space never matches. That is deliberate: a
deployment that has not wired its detector capability would otherwise
send every object to a model on a configuration mistake.
Cheap pre-checks on grades the platform already estimated, so a
hopeless candidate is refused before it costs a crop AND a call. An
unmeasured grade never fails a requirement — 'not measured' and
'measured as bad' are different claims.
